teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define a word, empty word Omega, prefix and truncation depth before history-space notation. Use a labeled binary classroom alphabet{a, b}; keep the source eight-letter alphabetB8 distinct and do not invent its missing physical labeling.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Depth<=2 binary words areOmega, a, b, aa, ab, ba, bb:7 orthogonal labels. Prefixa sends Omega->a, b->ab; removing a first a is the partial inverse, while removing a from ba gives zero in the linear operator model.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: At depth<=1 keep Omega, a, b. Prefix b sends Omega->b; at depth 2 it sends a->ba, b->bb. The empty word is a state label, not zero amplitude. An amplitude ledger retains every word and signed/complex coefficient.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A finite cutoff must state how terminal words are handled. The sourceF_hist=l²(B8*) includes all finite words and an empty-word root; it is not this 7-state matrix.

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach a three-state radial truncationS e0=e1, S e1=e2, S e2=0 and its transpose partial inverse. Compute both endpoint defects, then contrast a rectangular embedding. Keep square finite index and infinite unilateral-shift index separate.

worked_example.task_and_answer: S=[[0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]]. S†S=diag(1,1,0), SS†=diag(0,1,1); terminal and root defects each rank 1. kerS andkerS† each dimension 1, so finite index 0.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Forf=(2,3,4), Sf=(0,2,3), S†Sf=(2,3,0). Retain terminal4e2 to restoref. RectangularT:C²->C³, T(a, b)=(0, a, b) satisfiesT†T=I2 andTT†=diag(0,1,1); input(2,3) has norm squared 13 preserved.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The infinite unilateral shift onl²(N0) has no terminal defect, kerS=0, cokernel span e0 and index-1. Its isometry and index statements use that separate space/domain; they cannot be assigned to the3x3 truncation.

supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: Forf=(1,-2,5), Sf=(0,1,-2), S†Sf=(1,-2,0); addingretained(0,0,5) restoresf. ForT:C²->C³, T(1,-2)=(0,1,-2), norm squared 5 is preserved; T†T=I2.

course_map.assessment_target: Check idempotence and orthogonality of finite projectors

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach q_n=S^n P0(S†)^n using the explicit finite shift and root projector. Check self-adjointness, idempotence, orthogonality and ranks, including the first vanishing projector after the cutoff.

worked_example.task_and_answer: q0=diag(1,0,0), q1=diag(0,1,0), q2=diag(0,0,1), q3=0. The first three sumI3, all pairwise products vanish. On(1,2,3) they retain(1,0,0),(0,2,0),(0,0,3).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: On(-1,4,0), q0 gives(-1,0,0), q1(0,4,0), q2(0,0,0); retain the zero third coordinate and reconstruct. Eachq0..2 has rank 1, whileq3 rank 0; verifyq1²=q1 andq1q2=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The source wandering projection must lie in the defect space for the asserted orthogonality. A genericP cannot be inserted into the formula without checking this hypothesis.

course_map.title: Spatial handedness and a time direction

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Record spatial basis order, determinant sign, time direction and coframe order independently. Use a toy diagonal spatial basis to teach sign changes; do not reflect the authoritative left-handed Cell3 basis to make it right-handed.

worked_example.task_and_answer: SyntheticB=diag(1,2,-3) has det-6. Swapping the first two columns givesdet+6; reversing the time covector changes the four-dimensional orientation sign once more. Preserve both operations in the ledger.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: B=diag(2,1,-4) has det-8. Multiplying all spatial lengths bypositive 2 yields det-64 and preserves handedness. Reversing only the third axis flips the sign; label it as a changed orientation, not the same source basis.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A forward history choice is an additional temporal/coframe premise. Its sign is not inferred from a determinant magnitude or an internal exterior parity label.

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach a gradingG²=I withG=diag(1,-1), andPminus=(I-G)/2, Pplus=(I+G)/2. Use distinct two-state factors labeled(L, R) and(even, odd); form their correlation projector before discussing source chirality. Include the angular/spin supplement.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Pminus=diag(0,1), Pplus=diag(1,0) are orthogonal idempotents. On the independently ordered tensor labels(L, even),(L, odd),(R, even),(R, odd), Pi=diag(1,0,0,1). Pi(1,2,3,4)=(1,0,0,4), complement(0,2,3,0) is retained.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Pi(2,-1,0,3)=(2,0,0,3), complement(0,-1,0,0); reconstruct. Factor projectors commute because they act on separate factors. ForG=diag(1,-1) andXswap, GX+XG=0; verify bothP²=P andPminus Pplus=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The toy grading is not a complete spacetime Clifford representation. Correlating two labels does not equate them: spacetime chirality and exterior parity remain different factors.

supplemental_exercises.explanation: Define commutator[A, B]=AB-BA; distinguish pointwise real diagonal carry operators from general real matrices and supplied complex matrices. Teach a finite determinant existence witness without identifying a physical CP phase.
supplemental_exercises.worked_task_and_answer: diag(1,2) anddiag(3,4) commute. X=[[0,1],[1,0]], Y=[[0,-i],[i,0]] give[X, Y]=2i diag(1,-1), nonzero. This proves noncommutativity, not a measuredCP invariant.
supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: A=diag(1,-1), B=[[0,1+i],[1-i,0]] give[A, B]=[[0,2+2i],[-2+2i,0]]. Separately choose source-style positiveA0=diag(4,1,1/4), S=diag(2,1,1/2), D=diag(1, omega, omega²):Yu=S, Yd=D S^-1 D givesdet(YuYd)=1. Here both matrices are diagonal and commute, so determinant1 alone does not establish nonzeroCP.
supplemental_exercises.diagnostic_task_and_answer: The source real-carry obstruction assumes a commutative pointwise algebra; real matrices in general need not commute. A supplied positiveA and phase k are inputs; an existence witness does not predict CKM/PMNS values.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define a word, empty word Omega, prefix and truncation depth before history-space notation. Use a labeled binary classroom alphabet{a, b}; keep the source eight-letter alphabetB8 distinct and do not invent its missing physical labeling.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Depth<=2 binary words areOmega, a, b, aa, ab, ba, bb:7 orthogonal labels. Prefixa sends Omega->a, b->ab; removing a first a is the partial inverse, while removing a from ba gives zero in the linear operator model.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: At depth<=1 keep Omega, a, b. Prefix b sends Omega->b; at depth 2 it sends a->ba, b->bb. The empty word is a state label, not zero amplitude. An amplitude ledger retains every word and signed/complex coefficient.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A finite cutoff must state how terminal words are handled. The sourceF_hist=l²(B8*) includes all finite words and an empty-word root; it is not this 7-state matrix.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Forf=(2,3,4), Sf=(0,2,3), S†Sf=(2,3,0). Retain terminal4e2 to restoref. RectangularT:C²->C³, T(a, b)=(0, a, b) satisfiesT†T=I2 andTT†=diag(0,1,1); input(2,3) has norm squared 13 preserved.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The infinite unilateral shift onl²(N0) has no terminal defect, kerS=0, cokernel span e0 and index-1. Its isometry and index statements use that separate space/domain; they cannot be assigned to the3x3 truncation.

worked_example.task_and_answer: T(a, b)=(0, a, b) preservesnorm. T†(0,2,3)=(2,3), but no input reaches(1,0,0). ThusT†T=I2 whileTT† is a projection, notI3.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For output-space vector(5,2,3), T† gives(2,3); T T† gives(0,2,3), retained complement(5,0,0) restores the vector. Compare3x3 shift input(0,0,1), which maps0 and loses norm unless terminal coefficient is retained.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A one-sided inverse does not make a map reversible on its entire codomain. Specify the image and complement; do not claim time evolution from an isometry alone.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Teach q_n=S^n P0(S†)^n using the explicit finite shift and root projector. Check self-adjointness, idempotence, orthogonality and ranks, including the first vanishing projector after the cutoff.

worked_example.task_and_answer: q0=diag(1,0,0), q1=diag(0,1,0), q2=diag(0,0,1), q3=0. The first three sumI3, all pairwise products vanish. On(1,2,3) they retain(1,0,0),(0,2,0),(0,0,3).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: On(-1,4,0), q0 gives(-1,0,0), q1(0,4,0), q2(0,0,0); retain the zero third coordinate and reconstruct. Eachq0..2 has rank 1, whileq3 rank 0; verifyq1²=q1 andq1q2=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The source wandering projection must lie in the defect space for the asserted orthogonality. A genericP cannot be inserted into the formula without checking this hypothesis.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Record spatial basis order, determinant sign, time direction and coframe order independently. Use a toy diagonal spatial basis to teach sign changes; do not reflect the authoritative left-handed Cell3 basis to make it right-handed.

worked_example.task_and_answer: SyntheticB=diag(1,2,-3) has det-6. Swapping the first two columns givesdet+6; reversing the time covector changes the four-dimensional orientation sign once more. Preserve both operations in the ledger.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: B=diag(2,1,-4) has det-8. Multiplying all spatial lengths bypositive 2 yields det-64 and preserves handedness. Reversing only the third axis flips the sign; label it as a changed orientation, not the same source basis.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A forward history choice is an additional temporal/coframe premise. Its sign is not inferred from a determinant magnitude or an internal exterior parity label.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Teach a gradingG²=I withG=diag(1,-1), andPminus=(I-G)/2, Pplus=(I+G)/2. Use distinct two-state factors labeled(L, R) and(even, odd); form their correlation projector before discussing source chirality. Include the angular/spin supplement.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Pminus=diag(0,1), Pplus=diag(1,0) are orthogonal idempotents. On the independently ordered tensor labels(L, even),(L, odd),(R, even),(R, odd), Pi=diag(1,0,0,1). Pi(1,2,3,4)=(1,0,0,4), complement(0,2,3,0) is retained.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Pi(2,-1,0,3)=(2,0,0,3), complement(0,-1,0,0); reconstruct. Factor projectors commute because they act on separate factors. ForG=diag(1,-1) andXswap, GX+XG=0; verify bothP²=P andPminus Pplus=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The toy grading is not a complete spacetime Clifford representation. Correlating two labels does not equate them: spacetime chirality and exterior parity remain different factors.

supplemental_exercises.explanation: Define commutator[A, B]=AB-BA; distinguish pointwise real diagonal carry operators from general real matrices and supplied complex matrices. Teach a finite determinant existence witness without identifying a physical CP phase.
supplemental_exercises.worked_task_and_answer: diag(1,2) anddiag(3,4) commute. X=[[0,1],[1,0]], Y=[[0,-i],[i,0]] give[X, Y]=2i diag(1,-1), nonzero. This proves noncommutativity, not a measuredCP invariant.
supplemental_exercises.practice_task_and_answer: A=diag(1,-1), B=[[0,1+i],[1-i,0]] give[A, B]=[[0,2+2i],[-2+2i,0]]. Separately choose source-style positiveA0=diag(4,1,1/4), S=diag(2,1,1/2), D=diag(1, omega, omega²):Yu=S, Yd=D S^-1 D givesdet(YuYd)=1. Here both matrices are diagonal and commute, so determinant1 alone does not establish nonzeroCP.
supplemental_exercises.diagnostic_task_and_answer: The source real-carry obstruction assumes a commutative pointwise algebra; real matrices in general need not commute. A supplied positiveA and phase k are inputs; an existence witness does not predict CKM/PMNS values.
